    What is pop slang for?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    "Pop" in slang commonly means
    to suddenly appear (pop up), move quickly (pop over), or take drugs/medication. Other usages include a term for soda, "pops" as a term for a father, "pop off" as starting a fight or talking back, or to sell quickly/gain popularity. 
    Common "Pop" Slang Meanings: 
    • Pop Up/Pop In (Sudden Appearance/Short Visit): To appear unexpectedly, such as on social media (e.g., "they popped up in my DMs") or to visit briefly.
    • Pop Off (Reaction/Leaving): To leave suddenly, or to lose one's temper, start a fight, or talk back aggressively.
    • Pop (Drugs/Medicine) (Consumption): To take pills, medication, or drugs.
    • Pop (Music/Style) (Popularity): To become popular or well-known quickly.
    • Pops (Noun) (Father): A familiar, sometimes slightly disrespectful, term for one's father or an older man.
    • Pop (Soft Drink) (Regional): Primarily in the US Midwest/Canada, a term for a fizzy, carbonated beverage.
    • Pop (Sound) (Action): To make a sudden sound, or to shoot a gun.
